text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Military ruler General Sani Abacha restates at inaguration of committee to plan "Vision 2010" national development plan that 1998 date to hand over power to elected president stays.
- Nigeria blasts resolution being debated at U.N. general assembly on human rights in the country, plans counter proposal.

- Devaluation of CFA currency of central and West African French-speaking countries reduces patronage of Nigerian textiles in the sub region, says Senator Walid Jibrin, president of the Nigerian Textiles Manufacturers Association.
- Military ruler General Sani Abacha says he is convinced that "Vision 2010" programme will bring prosperity and political stability to Nigeria.
- Travel ban imposed by Saudi Arabia on Nigerians this year over meningitis epidemic will be relaxed in January, says Saudi consul-general in northern Kano city, Sheikh Usama Al-Jowhar.
- Improved metering system to measure oil exports to be installed next year at all Nigerian crude oil exporting terminals, says Wilson Dublin-Green, director of department of petroleum resources.
- Nigerian plastics manufacturers project they will earn $4 million from exports of plastics next year from current level of $250,000.
- Government of oil-producing Rivers state starts preliminary talks with Nigerian Stock Exchange to raise 400 million naira through debenture stock next year.
- Conflicting signals on next month's local council poll as government insists they must hold while transition committee advises it should be postponed, according to political sources.
- National carrier Nigeria Airways goes to court in London to retrieve its DC-10 aircraft impounded in the British capital over debt it owes a British finance firm.
- Cotton farmers lose out as prices of the commodity drops by 40 percent within first month of harvest season.
